sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: OOP questions dominate the first 15 minutes of every Python fresher technical round. Interviewers ask them in sequence — class → object → __init__ → encapsulation → inheritance → polymorphism — and stop when you hesitate. Know them in order.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Class = blueprint. Object = instance built from blueprint.**

The four pillars map to Python as follows:
- **Encapsulation** — `_protected` (convention) and `__private` (name mangling). Not enforced by the language, but signals intent.
- **Inheritance** — `class Child(Parent)`. MRO (Method Resolution Order) via `__mro__` resolves diamond inheritance.
- **Polymorphism** — same method name, different behaviour. Python uses duck typing: if it has the method, it works.
- **Abstraction** — `abc.ABC` + `@abstractmethod`. Forces subclasses to implement the contract.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **`__init__` vs `__new__`** — `__init__` initialises; `__new__` creates. For freshers: only `__init__` matters.
- **`self`** — explicit first parameter of every instance method. Not a keyword — just a convention (but always use `self`).
- **`super()`** — calls the parent class method. Essential in `__init__` chains.
- **`@classmethod` vs `@staticmethod`** — classmethod receives `cls`, staticmethod receives nothing. Both skip `self`.
- **`isinstance()` vs `type()`** — `isinstance` respects inheritance; `type` does exact match.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the difference between a class variable and an instance variable?'** — class vars are shared; instance vars are per-object. Mutation via instance creates a shadow copy.
- **'What is MRO?'** — C3 linearisation. `ClassName.__mro__` shows the resolution order.
- **'What is duck typing?'** — if it walks like a duck and quacks, Python treats it as a duck. No interface declaration needed.
- **'Can Python do multiple inheritance?'** — yes, but MRO handles ambiguity. Java can't (interfaces only).

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"The four pillars in Python work like this — [encapsulation with single/double underscore], [inheritance with super() and MRO], [polymorphism through method overriding and duck typing], [abstraction with abc.ABC]. The distinction I find freshers often miss is X."*
